repo_notes.content: Generate separate, fully localized en and zh wikis. The English titles and parent names in pages are canonical outline identifiers, not text to copy into every locale. For en, write all user-facing titles, navigation, headings, summaries, diagrams, and prose in English. For zh / zh-CN / zh-Hans, translate them consistently into Simplified Chinese. Use these six Chinese top-level titles, in order: 入门指南, 核心 TLS 模块, 抓取模式, 进阶使用, 架构与探针开发, 构建、测试与发布. Translate Other Modules as 其他模块. Preserve product names, CLI flags, API paths, code identifiers, and standard technical terms such as TLS, eBPF, text, keylog, and pcapng. Check every generated page for wrong-language titles or prose.

Create exactly the six top-level sections in pages, with no extra top-level section. The first four sections contain 21 user-facing pages; the last two contain 9 developer-facing pages. Aim for about 70% of total explanatory content for users and 30% for developers, not just the page-count ratio. User pages explain selection, prerequisites, runnable workflows, expected output, interpretation, and troubleshooting. Developer pages explain architecture, event ABI, lifecycle, output routing, builds, tests, and extension. Keep NSS/NSPR, Bash, Zsh, MySQL/MariaDB, and PostgreSQL only in the single Other Modules page under Advanced Usage. Give no non-core probe its own page or chapter elsewhere.

The core of this wiki is tls (OpenSSL/BoringSSL), gotls, and gnutls. Spend most user-facing space on using these three commands and choosing among text, keylog, and pcapng. Each core module and each mode needs verified commands, required target or interface setup, expected artifact, a way to confirm success, and relevant limitations. Explain that text shows captured plaintext events, keylog provides TLS secrets for a separate packet capture, and pcapng contains packet blocks plus an embedded TLS Decryption Secrets Block. Do not imply keylog alone contains packets or pcapng is only a keylog file.

Verify facts against current source code, README, docs/agent/architecture.md, and docs/agent/output-pipeline.md. For tls, gotls, and gnutls, -m selects text, keylog, or pcap/pcapng representation; --eventaddr selects the primary captured-event destination; --logaddr carries operational logs only. Explain the legacy --keylogfile and --pcapfile aliases and mode-specific destination and rotation rules accurately. Do not invent commands, supported versions, or performance numbers. Do not put source-file links or code citations in summaries or user-facing explanatory text. Mermaid labels must describe concepts, not file paths or Markdown links.

# Getting Started

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

## Purpose and Scope
eCapture (旁观者) is an eBPF-based tool designed to capture SSL/TLS plaintext communication, perform command-line auditing, and monitor database queries without requiring a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) proxy or custom CA certificate installation [README.md:5-8](), [README.md:59-67](). This entry point guides users through system prerequisites, selecting the appropriate TLS capture module (`tls`, `gotls`, or `gnutls`), and executing your first plaintext, keylog, or pcapng capture workflow.

Sources: `[README.md:5-8]`, `[README.md:59-67]`

---

### Title: Core TLS Command Routing to Probe Factory
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph CLI ["CLI Command Space"]
        A["opensslCmd"] -->|"cli/cmd/tls.go:29-48"| D["runConfiguredProbe"]
        B["gotlsCmd"] -->|"cli/cmd/gotls.go:28-43"| D
        C["gnutlsCmd"] -->|"cli/cmd/gnutls.go:33-49"| D
    end
    subgraph Factory ["Code Entity Space"]
        D -->|"factory.ProbeTypeOpenSSL"| E["opensslProbe.NewConfig"]
        D -->|"factory.ProbeTypeGoTLS"| F["gotlsProbe.NewConfig"]
        D -->|"factory.ProbeTypeGnuTLS"| G["gnutlsProbe.NewConfig"]
    end
```
Sources: `[cli/cmd/tls.go:29-48]`, `[cli/cmd/gotls.go:28-43]`, `[cli/cmd/gnutls.go:33-49]`

---

## 1.1 Requirements and Installation
eCapture supports Linux on x86_64 (kernel 4.18+), aarch64 (kernel 5.5+), and LoongArch64 (kernel 6.6+), as well as Android on x86_64 and aarch64 [README.md:34-38](). Execution requires root privileges or specific Linux capabilities to load eBPF programs and attach uprobes/TC classifiers [README.md:34-38](). For complete details on kernel BTF requirements, capability configuration, and environment setup, see [Requirements and Installation](#1.1).

Sources: `[README.md:34-38]`, `[README.md:70-98]`

---

## 1.2 Choosing a TLS Probe
Depending on your target application stack, eCapture provides three core TLS capture modules:
- **`tls`**: Targets OpenSSL, LibreSSL, and BoringSSL shared libraries or statically linked binaries [README.md:131](), [cli/cmd/tls.go:29-32]().
- **`gotls`**: Targets Go binaries built with Go's native `crypto/tls` package [README.md:127](), [cli/cmd/gotls.go:28-32]().
- **`gnutls`**: Targets applications linked against the GnuTLS cryptographic library [README.md:126](), [cli/cmd/gnutls.go:33-36]().

For a comprehensive decision matrix comparing targets, library paths, and output capabilities, see [Choosing a TLS Probe](#1.2).

Sources: `[README.md:126-131]`, `[cli/cmd/tls.go:29-32]`, `[cli/cmd/gotls.go:28-32]`, `[cli/cmd/gnutls.go:33-36]`

---

### Title: Output Pipeline Mode Selection
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph Modes ["Capture Mode Space"]
        M1["text (-m text)"] --> O1["Plaintext Stream"]
        M2["keylog (-m keylog)"] --> O2["NSS Key Log File"]
        M3["pcapng (-m pcap)"] --> O3["Packets + Decryption Secrets Block"]
    end
    subgraph Config ["Configuration Flags"]
        F1["--eventaddr"] --> O1
        F2["--keylogfile"] --> O2
        F3["--pcapfile"] --> O3
    end
```
Sources: `[cli/cmd/tls.go:53-55]`, `[cli/cmd/gotls.go:49-51]`, `[cli/cmd/gnutls.go:53-55]`

---

## 1.3 First OpenSSL and BoringSSL Capture
The `tls` command automatically discovers system OpenSSL libraries or accepts explicit paths via `--libssl` [README.md:136-139](), [cli/cmd/tls.go:51](). Running in text mode prints decrypted HTTPS requests and responses directly to the console [README.md:106-116](). For verified end-to-end command examples, traffic generators, and transitions to keylog and pcapng workflows, see [First OpenSSL and BoringSSL Capture](#1.3).

Sources: `[README.md:100-116]`, `[cli/cmd/tls.go:29-51]`

---

## 1.4 First GoTLS Capture
The `gotls` command targets Go binaries by specifying the compiled binary path via `--elfpath` [cli/cmd/gotls.go:46](). It hooks Go's internal TLS connection functions to extract plaintext traffic [README.md:127](). For verified text-mode commands, required flags, expected events, and advanced output bindings, see [First GoTLS Capture](#1.4).

Sources: `[README.md:127]`, `[cli/cmd/gotls.go:28-46]`

---

## 1.5 First GnuTLS Capture
The `gnutls` command captures plaintext from applications linked with GnuTLS [README.md:126](), [cli/cmd/gnutls.go:33-36](). It supports explicit library paths (`--gnutls`) and version specifiers (`--ssl_version`) across Linux and Termux/Android environments [cli/cmd/gnutls.go:52-57](). For complete instructions, version checks, and output examples, see [First GnuTLS Capture](#1.5).

Sources: `[README.md:126]`, `[cli/cmd/gnutls.go:33-57]`

## Purpose and Scope
This page defines the host environment requirements, kernel configurations, privilege requirements (root or Linux capabilities), and installation procedures required to run eCapture. It details the runtime dependencies for the three core TLS capture modules (`tls` for OpenSSL/BoringSSL, `gotls` for Go native TLS, and `gnutls` for GnuTLS) and explains the interface prerequisites specific to `pcapng` capture modes.

Sources: [`docs/compilation.md:26-37](), [`docs/minimum-privileges.md:5-34]()

---

## Supported Platforms and Architectures
eCapture relies on eBPF uprobes, tracepoints, and Traffic Control (TC) hooks, which impose strict kernel version and architecture constraints.

| Architecture | Minimum Linux Kernel | Android Support | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x86_64` | Kernel 4.18+ | Supported | Full CO-RE and non-CO-RE support |
| `aarch64` (`arm64`) | Kernel 5.5+ | Supported | Requires Android 12+ typically |
| `LoongArch64` (`loong64`) | Kernel 6.6+ | Not Supported | Requires LLVM 18+ and specific sysroots |

Sources: [`docs/compilation.md:28-30](), [`docs/minimum-privileges.md:124-126]()

---

## Kernel and BTF Requirements
eCapture operates in two bytecode modes: CO-RE (Compile Once – Run Everywhere) using BPF Type Format (BTF) and non-CO-RE (fallback compilation using local kernel headers).

### BTF Detection Logic
At startup, eCapture checks whether kernel BTF is enabled by inspecting `/sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux` or scanning fallback directories for kernel ELF images via `checkKernelBTF()` [pkg/util/ebpf/bpf.go:89-98](). If BTF is absent, it falls back to inspecting kernel configuration files (`/proc/config.gz`, `/boot/config-*`) for `CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF` [pkg/util/ebpf/bpf_linux.go:28-31]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    Start["IsEnableBTF()"] --> CheckBTF["checkKernelBTF()"]
    CheckBTF -->|Exists| FoundBTF["Use CO-RE Bytecode"]
    CheckBTF -->|Missing| ReadConfig["GetSystemConfig()"]
    ReadConfig --> CheckConfig["CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF == y?"]
    CheckConfig -->|Yes| FoundBTF
    CheckConfig -->|No| Fallback["Non-CO-RE / nocore mode"]

    sub5["pkg/util/ebpf/bpf.go:118-143"]
    sub6["pkg/util/ebpf/bpf_linux.go:48-80"]
```
Sources: [`pkg/util/ebpf/bpf.go:89-143](), [`pkg/util/ebpf/bpf_linux.go:48-80]()

### Mandatory Kernel Configurations
Regardless of BTF, the target kernel must have the following options enabled, verified by `IsEnableBPF()` [pkg/util/ebpf/bpf.go:146-170]():
* `CONFIG_BPF`
* `CONFIG_UPROBES`
* `CONFIG_ARCH_SUPPORTS_UPROBES`

Sources: [`pkg/util/ebpf/bpf.go:30-44](), [`pkg/util/ebpf/bpf.go:146-170]()

---

## Privileges, Root, and Capabilities
Loading eBPF programs, attaching uprobes to shared libraries, and binding TC classifiers require elevated privileges.

### Linux Capabilities Breakdown
Starting with Linux 5.8, eBPF privileges were unbundled from `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`. The required capabilities vary by kernel version and operating mode:

| eCapture Mode | Kernel >= 5.8 Required Capabilities | Kernel < 5.8 Required Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `CAP_BPF` + `CAP_PERFMON` + `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` | `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` |
| `keylog` | `CAP_BPF` + `CAP_PERFMON` + `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` | `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` |
| `pcapng` | `CAP_BPF` + `CAP_PERFMON` + `CAP_NET_ADMIN` + `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` | `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` + `CAP_NET_ADMIN` |

Sources: [`docs/minimum-privileges.md:5-34]()

### Capability Assignment via `setcap`
To run eCapture without full `root` or `sudo` privileges, assign extended attributes to the binary:

```bash
# For kernel >= 5.8 in pcapng mode
sudo setcap 'cap_bpf,cap_perfmon,cap_net_admin,cap_sys_ptrace=eip' /usr/local/bin/ecapture

# Verify capabilities
getcap /usr/local/bin/ecapture
```

Sources: [`docs/minimum-privileges.md:45-73]()

```mermaid
graph TD
    Init["CLI Startup"] --> CheckKernel["Check Kernel Version"]
    CheckKernel --> CheckCaps["Check Process Capabilities"]
    CheckCaps -->|Insufficient| ErrorExit["Exit: missing CAP_BPF / CAP_SYS_ADMIN"]
    CheckCaps -->|Sufficient| AttachProbes["Load eBPF and Attach Uprobes"]

    sub7["docs/minimum-privileges.md:120-135"]
```
Sources: [`docs/minimum-privileges.md:120-135]()

---

## pcapng Interface Prerequisites
When operating in `pcapng` mode (`-m pcap` or `-m pcapng`), eCapture intercepts network packets via Traffic Control (TC) ebpf hooks on a specified network interface (`-i <interface>`) and injects decrypted payload secrets into a `Decryption Secrets Block (DSB)`.

* **Prerequisites**:
  * `CAP_NET_ADMIN` capability (or running as root).
  * A valid, active network interface name (e.g., `eth0`, `ens160`, `wlan0`).
  * When running inside Docker, `--net=host` is mandatory to access and attach TC filters to host network interfaces.

Sources: [`docs/minimum-privileges.md:13-34](), [`docs/minimum-privileges.md:113-118]()

---

## Module-Specific Prerequisites
The three core TLS capture modules target different underlying runtimes and shared library implementations:

1. **`tls` (OpenSSL and BoringSSL)**:
   * Targets dynamic libraries: `libssl.so` (OpenSSL 1.0.x, 1.1.x, 3.0+) or BoringSSL (Android / Chrome / custom binaries).
   * Requires symbol resolution for functions such as `SSL_do_handshake`, `SSL_read`, and `SSL_write`.
2. **`gotls` (Go Native TLS)**:
   * Targets compiled Go binaries using `crypto/tls`.
   * Requires DWARF symbol tables or function table offsets to locate internal Go TLS structures (e.g., `crypto/tls.(*Conn).read` / `write`).
3. **`gnutls` (GnuTLS)**:
   * Targets applications linked against `libgnutls.so`.
   * Requires compatible version bindings for GnuTLS handshake and record-layer state functions.

Sources: [`docs/compilation.md:132-154]()

---

## Installation and Compilation from Source
eCapture is built using Go and Clang/LLVM.

### Build Toolchain Prerequisites
* **Golang**: 1.26.0 or newer
* **Clang / LLVM**: 9.0 or newer (LLVM 18 required for LoongArch64)
* **CMake**: 3.18.4 or newer
* **Libelf**: `libelf-dev`

### Compilation Commands
```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/gojue/ecapture.git
cd ecapture
make
bin/ecapture
```

Sources: [`docs/compilation.md:33-67]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page provides a technical comparison and decision framework for selecting the appropriate eCapture TLS probe (`tls`, `gotls`, or `gnutls`). Choosing the correct probe depends on the target application's underlying cryptographic library or language runtime, the operating system platform (Linux vs. Android), and the desired output representation (`text`, `keylog`, or `pcap`/`pcapng`).

Sources: [cli/cmd/tls.go:29-48](), [cli/cmd/gotls.go:28-43](), [cli/cmd/gnutls.go:33-49]()

---

## Core TLS Probes Decision Matrix

The following decision table maps application runtimes and binary characteristics to the correct eCapture CLI subcommand, internal probe factory type, and bytecode targets.

| Target Application Stack | Target Library / Binary | Supported Versions | Supported Platforms | CLI Command | Factory Probe Type | Primary eBPF Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **OpenSSL / BoringSSL** | `libssl.so`, static binaries, Android Conscrypt (`libssl.so`) | OpenSSL 1.0.x, 1.1.x, 3.x+; BoringSSL | Linux (`x86_64`, `aarch64`, `loongarch64`), Android (`x86_64`, `aarch64`) | `ecapture tls` | `factory.ProbeTypeOpenSSL` | `kern/openssl*_kern.c`, `kern/boringssl*_kern.c` |
| **Go Native TLS** | Go compiled ELF binaries (`crypto/tls`) | Go 1.17 – Go 1.26+ (v1/v2 ABI discovery) | Linux (`x86_64`, `aarch64`, `loongarch64`), Android (`x86_64`, `aarch64`) | `ecapture gotls` | `factory.ProbeTypeGoTLS` | `kern/gotls_kern.c` |
| **GnuTLS** | `libgnutls.so` | GnuTLS 3.6.x, 3.7.x, 3.8.x | Linux (`x86_64`, `aarch64`, `loongarch64`), Android Termux (`aarch64`) | `ecapture gnutls` | `factory.ProbeTypeGnuTLS` | `kern/gnutls_*_kern.c` |

Sources: [cli/cmd/tls.go:29-61](), [cli/cmd/gotls.go:28-55](), [cli/cmd/gnutls.go:33-60](), [docs/agent/architecture.md:37-49]()

---

## Probe Selection Architecture

The diagram below bridges natural language selection criteria to concrete code entities across the CLI parser, factory registry, and probe initialization packages.

```mermaid
graph TD
    CLIInput["CLI Input Arguments"] --> ParseCmd{"Command Parser"}
    ParseCmd -->|"`ecapture tls`"| OpenSSLConfig["opensslConfig openssl/config.go"]
    ParseCmd -->|"`ecapture gotls`"| GoTLSConfig["gotlsConfig gotls/config.go"]
    ParseCmd -->|"`ecapture gnutls`"| GnuTLSConfig["gnutlsConfig gnutls/config.go"]
    
    OpenSSLConfig --> FactoryReg["factory.CreateProbe() internal/factory/"]
    GoTLSConfig --> FactoryReg
    GnuTLSConfig --> FactoryReg
```

## Detailed Probe Profiles

### 1. OpenSSL and BoringSSL Probe (`tls`)
* **Use Case**: Applications dynamically or statically linked against OpenSSL (such as Nginx, cURL, Python, Node.js, PHP) or Google BoringSSL (Android system apps, Chrome).
* **Key Flags**: `--libssl` to specify custom library paths [cli/cmd/tls.go:51](); `--ssl_version` to target specific ABI offsets [cli/cmd/tls.go:57](); `-m text|keylog|pcap` for output modes [cli/cmd/tls.go:53]().

### 2. Go Native TLS Probe (`gotls`)
* **Use Case**: Compiled Go binaries using Go's standard library `crypto/tls` package. Does not depend on OpenSSL.
* **Key Flags**: `--elfpath` (`-e`) to point to the target Go binary for symbol and register ABI discovery [cli/cmd/gotls.go:46](); `--perf-reorder` for high-throughput ordering [cli/cmd/gotls.go:47]().
* **Implementation Details**: Resolves Go internal function symbols such as `crypto/tls.(*Conn).Read`, `crypto/tls.(*Conn).writeRecordLocked`, and `crypto/tls.(*Config).writeKeyLog` [internal/probe/gotls/gotls_probe.go:47-50]().

### 3. GnuTLS Probe (`gnutls`)
* **Use Case**: Applications compiled against the GnuTLS library (common in enterprise Linux distributions and Termux on Android).
* **Key Flags**: `--gnutls` to specify `libgnutls.so` path [cli/cmd/gnutls.go:52](); `--ssl_version` for GnuTLS version mapping [cli/cmd/gnutls.go:57]().

## Purpose and Scope

This page provides a verified end-to-end guide for capturing TLS traffic from Go native binaries using eCapture's `gotls` module in text mode. Unlike OpenSSL or GnuTLS—which rely on dynamic shared libraries (`libssl.so` or `libgnutls.so`)—Go applications statically link their own TLS stack (`crypto/tls`) and use custom calling conventions and internal data structures. 

This guide covers target binary selection, required CLI flags (`--elfpath`, `-m text`, `--eventaddr`, `--logaddr`), the expected event payload structure, and transitions to keylog and pcapng workflows [test/e2e/linux/gotls_test.sh:53-129]().

Sources: `test/e2e/linux/gotls_test.sh:53-129`

## Target Binary Preparation and Prerequisites

Before invoking the `gotls` probe, ensure your target Go application meets the following criteria:
1. **ELF Binary Path**: eCapture requires access to the Go binary's ELF file via `--elfpath` or target Process ID (`--pid`) to resolve symbol tables and function offsets for `crypto/tls.(*Conn).Read` and `crypto/tls.(*Conn).Write`.
2. **Symbol Tables**: Stripped binaries lacking Go symbol tables (`go.itab` or function names) may require symbol restoration or pointing to an unstripped compilation artifact.
3. **Kernel & Privileges**: Requires Linux kernel 4.18+ (x86_64) or 5.5+ (ARM64) with BTF support, running with root privileges (`sudo`) [test/e2e/linux/common.sh:30-47]().

Sources: `test/e2e/linux/common.sh:30-47`, `test/e2e/linux/gotls_test.sh:53-70`

## Verified End-to-End GoTLS Text-Mode Command

To capture plaintext events from a Go HTTPS client or server in text mode, execute the following verified command [test/e2e/linux/gotls_test.sh:57-70]():

```bash
sudo ./bin/ecapture gotls \
    --elfpath /path/to/go_https_client \
    --model text \
    --eventaddr ./gotls_events.log \
    --logaddr ./gotls_operational.log
```

### Flag Reference
- `gotls`: Selects the Go native TLS capture module.
- `--elfpath`: Specifies the path to the compiled Go executable containing `crypto/tls` symbols [test/e2e/linux/gotls_test.sh:57]().
- `-m text` (or `--model text`): Selects text representation, streaming decoded plaintext records to the designated output [test/e2e/linux/gotls_test.sh:57]().
- `--eventaddr`: Routes captured plaintext data events to a file, stdout, or network sink [test/e2e/linux/gotls_test.sh:57]().
- `--logaddr`: Directs operational lifecycle logs (initialization, attachment status, errors) separately from event payloads, ensuring output isolation [test/e2e/linux/gotls_test.sh:57]().

Sources: `test/e2e/linux/gotls_test.sh:57-70`

## Transition to Keylog and pcapng Workflows

Once you have verified text-mode capture, you can switch representation models using the `-m` flag without altering target setup:

1. **Keylog Mode (`-m keylog`)**: Extracts TLS master secrets or traffic secrets and writes them in NSS Key Log format. This allows a separate packet capture (`tcpdump` or `tshark`) to decrypt traffic offline [test/e2e/linux/gotls_test.sh:72-108]().
2. **pcapng Mode (`-m pcapng`)**: Automatically combines packet capture on a specified interface (`--ifname lo`) with captured TLS secrets, embedding them into a `pcapng` file with a TLS Decryption Secrets Block (DSB) [test/e2e/linux/gotls_test.sh:110-129]().

## Prerequisites and Target Discovery

Before running a GnuTLS capture, you must locate the target shared library (e.g., `libgnutls.so`) on your Linux system and verify its version. GnuTLS relies on hardcoded structure offset maps compiled into eBPF bytecode objects corresponding to specific minor and patch releases (such as `3.6.12`, `3.7.3`, `3.7.7`, `3.8.4`, and `3.8.7`).

1. **Locate the Library**: Use `ldconfig` or package managers to find the absolute path of `libgnutls.so`:

   Typical paths include `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30` or `/usr/lib64/libgnutls.so`.

2. **Verify Version Compatibility**: Inspect your GnuTLS version using `pkg-config` or library queries:
   ```sh
   pkg-config --modversion gnutls
   ```
   Ensure the version matches one of the supported bytecode definitions in `kern/`.


2. **验证版本兼容性**：使用 `pkg-config` 或库查询检查 GnuTLS 版本：

## 验证过的端到端文本模式命令

文本模式 (`-m text`) 将 uprobe 附加到 GnuTLS 记录层函数（`gnutls_record_send` 和 `gnutls_record_recv`），拦截缓冲区，并将解码后的明文事件直接输出到标准输出。

### 命令执行

以 root 权限运行 `ecapture`，指定目标 GnuTLS 库路径、检测到的版本以及文本捕获模式：

```sh
sudo ./bin/ecapture gnutls --libgnutls /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30 --gversion 3.7.7 -m text
```

### 预期事件输出

当目标应用程序（例如 `gnutls-cli` 或自定义客户端）执行 TLS 握手并交换数据时，`ecapture` 会将结构化事件记录打印到 stdout：

```text
2/4 [I] time="202X-XX-XXTTT:HH:MM:SSZ" level=info msg="GnuTLS probe started successfully"
2/4 [I] event type: 3, PID: 12345, TID: 12345, UID: 0, Comm: gnutls-cli
2/4 [I] Plaintext Read/Write (Length: 51):
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
User-Agent: GnuTLS
```

## Target Library Discovery and `--libssl`

The OpenSSL probe initializes by locating the target shared library (`libssl.so`) hosting the SSL/TLS functions (`SSL_read`, `SSL_write`, `SSL_do_handshake`, or BoringSSL keylog hooks). 

If the user does not supply an explicit path via `--libssl`, `ecapture` performs automated platform-specific discovery:
- **Linux:** Scans standard system library paths and inspects loaded process maps or shared objects.
- **Android:** Searches APEX and system paths such as `/apex/com.android.conscrypt/lib64/libssl.so`, `/apex/com.android.conscrypt/lib/libssl.so`, `/system/lib64/libssl.so`, and `/system/lib/libssl.so`.

## Android BoringSSL Support and Symbol Resolution

On Android platforms running BoringSSL, standard export symbols for master secret logging may be stripped or optimized out. `ecapture` handles this by parsing the `.gnu_debugdata` section containing an XZ-compressed mini debug symbol table.

The function `findBoringSSLKeylogAddress` opens the ELF binary, extracts `.gnu_debugdata`, decompresses the XZ stream using `github.com/ulikunitz/xz`, parses the inner ELF symbols, and locates the internal `_ZN4bssl14ssl_log_secretEPK6ssl_stPKcNS_4SpanIKhEE` (`bssl::ssl_log_secret`) function address.

```
+-----------------------+     +----------------------+     +-------------------------+
| ELF File Opening      |---->| Read .gnu_debugdata  |---->| XZ Decompression Stream |
| (elf.Open)            |     | (lib.Section)        |     | (xz.NewReader)          |
+-----------------------+     +----------------------+     +-------------------------+
                                                                        |
                                                                        v
+-----------------------+     +----------------------+     +-------------------------+
| Compute File Offset   |<----| Match Symbol         |<----| Parse Inner ELF Symbols |
| (executableFileOffset)|     | (boringSSLKeylogSym) |     | (elf.NewFile)           |
+-----------------------+     +----------------------+     +-------------------------+
```

This page explains the technical implementation, configuration considerations, symbol and calling-convention mechanics, and verified operational workflows for the `gotls` capture module in eCapture. The `gotls` module traces native TLS connections in Go binaries via eBPF uprobes and uretprobes without requiring external cryptographic libraries like OpenSSL.

## 1. Purpose and Scope

The `gotls` module targets Go applications compiled with the standard library `crypto/tls` package. Because Go binaries statically link their TLS implementation and runtime support, traditional dynamic library interception (such as hooking `libssl`) is ineffective. Instead, eCapture attaches eBPF probes directly to Go runtime functions responsible for reading, writing, and logging keys within the target ELF binary.

Supported capabilities include:
- **Text Mode (`-m text`)**: Decodes application-layer plaintext data read from and written to Go TLS connections along with network tuples (IP, port, file descriptor, process metadata).
- **Keylog Mode (`-m keylog`)**: Extracts NSS-compatible key log secrets (`CLIENT_RANDOM`, etc.) when `crypto/tls.(*Config).writeKeyLog` is invoked.
- **pcapng Mode (`-m pcap` / `-m pcapng`)**: Captures packet blocks from a network interface while embedding a TLS Decryption Secrets Block containing the extracted keys for direct Wireshark inspection.

Sources: [internal/probe/gotls/gotls_probe.go:46-50](), [internal/probe/gotls/event.go:33-74]()

## 2. Go Binary Selection and Prerequisites

To successfully attach probes to a Go binary, eCapture requires the target process or ELF file path to contain Go debug and symbol metadata (specifically, `.gopclntab` or section data). Stripped binaries lacking symbol tables require external symbol maps or symbols preserved via linker flags (`-ldflags="-w=false"`).

### Version and Architecture Support
- **Supported Go Versions**: Go 1.16 through recent releases (including Go 1.17+ register-based ABI and Go 1.18+ text-relative function offset tables).
- **Architectures**: AMD64 (`__TARGET_ARCH_x86`), ARM64 (`__TARGET_ARCH_arm64`), and LoongArch (`__TARGET_ARCH_loongarch`).
- **Target Specification**: Specified via the CLI using `--pid` for running processes or `--elf` for static analysis and binary attachment setup.

## 3. Symbol Resolution and Calling Conventions

Go uses specialized calling conventions that evolved significantly between Go 1.16 and Go 1.17+. Understanding these conventions is critical for eBPF argument extraction.

### Hooked Functions
The `gotls` module attaches probes to three core `crypto/tls` internal methods:
1. **Read**: `crypto/tls.(*Conn).Read` — intercepts incoming decrypted application data.
2. **Write**: `crypto/tls.(*Conn).writeRecordLocked` — intercepts outgoing application data before encryption.
3. **Keylog**: `crypto/tls.(*Config).writeKeyLog` — intercepts TLS master secrets and random values.

Sources: [internal/probe/gotls/gotls_probe.go:46-50]()

### ABI Considerations (Register vs. Stack)
- **Stack-based ABI (Go 1.16 and older)**: Function parameters are passed via the stack relative to the stack pointer register (`SP`). Argument retrieval reads from `PT_REGS_SP(ctx) + (index * 8)`.
- **Register-based ABI (Go 1.17 and newer)**: Function parameters are passed via CPU registers (`AX`, `BX`, `CX`, `DI`, `SI`, `R8`, `R9`, `R10` on AMD64). The macro `GO_PARAM1` through `GO_PARAM8` extracts values directly from register definitions or via CO-RE helpers.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Calling Convention Space"
        H1["Go Function Entry crypto/tls.(*Conn).Read"] --> H2{"Is Register ABI? config.IsRegisterABI"}
        H2 -->|Yes Go 1.17+| H3["Extract via CPU Registers kern/go_argument.h:GO_PARAM1"]
        H2 -->|No Go 1.16-| H4["Extract via Stack Offset kern/go_argument.h:go_get_argument_by_stack"]
        H3 --> H5["Read TLS Connection Pointer (*tls.Conn)"]
        H4 --> H5
        H5 --> H6["Extract net.netFD and File Descriptor kern/gotls_kern.c:get_netfd_ptr_from_tls_conn"]
    end
```
*Figure 3.1: Calling convention resolution bridging natural language configuration to eBPF code structures.*

Sources: [kern/go_argument.h:22-128](), [kern/gotls_kern.c:110-146]()

## 4. Implementation and Data Flow

When an application invokes `crypto/tls.(*Conn).Read` or `writeRecordLocked`, the attached uprobe executes in kernel context, extracts connection metadata (`netFD`, source/destination IPs, ports, file descriptors), and copies the payload into a per-CPU eBPF array map (`gte_context_gen`).

### eBPF Data Structure (`struct go_tls_event`)
Events are structured uniformly in kernel space and transmitted to userspace via BPF perf event arrays (`events` and `mastersecret_go_events`):

| Offset | Field Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | `ts_ns` | `u64` | Monotonic timestamp (`bpf_ktime_get_ns`) |
| 8 | `pid` / `tid` | `u32` / `u32` | Process and Thread IDs |
| 16 | `data_len` | `s32` | Payload length |
| 20 | `event_type` | `u8` | `0` = Write, `1` = Read |
| 24 | `fd` | `u32` | Underlying network file descriptor |
| 28 | `src_ip` / `dst_ip` | `u8[16]` | Source and destination IP addresses (IPv4/IPv6) |
| 44 / 64 | `src_port` / `dst_port` | `u16` / `u16` | Source and destination ports |
| 68 | `comm` | `char[16]` | Process command name |
| 84 | `data` | `char[...]` | Payload buffer |

Sources: [kern/gotls_kern.c:33-50](), [internal/probe/gotls/event.go:33-74]()

## 6. Expected Results and Interpretation

When evaluating captures from `gotls`:
1. **Text Mode**: Validates that plaintext bytes match application requests/responses. Ensure the binary is not stripped or build IDs match.
2. **Keylog Mode**: Produces standard NSS key log lines. These can be combined with standard `tcpdump` captures in Wireshark via **Preferences > Protocols > TLS > (Pre)-Master-Secret log filename**.
3. **pcapng Mode**: Generates a self-contained artifact (`.pcapng`) containing both link-layer packets and the TLS Decryption Secrets Block (DSB), allowing immediate inspection in Wireshark without manual key file configuration.

## Overview and Scope

The GnuTLS capture module (`gnutls`) provides non-invasive plaintext, keylog, and packet capture capabilities for applications dynamically or statically linked against the GNU Transport Layer Security (GnuTLS) library (`libgnutls.so`) [internal/probe/gnutls/config.go:63-75](). Unlike OpenSSL or GoTLS, GnuTLS relies heavily on internal structure layout variations across minor and patch releases. Consequently, eCapture employs version-specific eBPF bytecode objects matched to the target library version detected during initialization [internal/probe/gnutls/config.go:33-61]().

Sources: [internal/probe/gnutls/config.go:33-75]()

---

## Target Library and Version Support

The target library is typically located at standard system paths such as `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30` [internal/probe/gnutls/config.go:63-75](). During startup, `Config.Validate()` inspects the target binary to determine the exact GnuTLS version string (ranging from `3.6.12` to `3.8.9`) [internal/probe/gnutls/config.go:101-143](). 

The mapping from detected version to compiled eBPF object is managed by `gnuTLSVersionAssets` [internal/probe/gnutls/config.go:33-61](). For example, versions `3.8.4` through `3.8.6` resolve to `gnutls_3_8_4_kern.o`, while `3.8.7` through `3.8.9` resolve to `gnutls_3_8_7_kern.o` [internal/probe/gnutls/config.go:55-61]().

| `3.7.0` - `3.7.11` | `gnutls_3_7_0_kern.o` / `gnutls_3_7_7_kern.o` [internal/probe/gnutls/config.go:39-50]() | `gnutls_record_send`, `gnutls_record_recv`, session key extractors |

| `3.8.4` - `3.8.6` | `gnutls_3_8_4_kern.o` [internal/probe/gnutls/config.go:55-57]() | `gnutls_record_send`, `gnutls_record_recv`, session key extractors |

## Platform Limits and Prerequisites

- **Operating Systems**: Linux only (`x86_64`, `aarch64`, `loongarch64`).
- **Android Restriction**: The GnuTLS module is excluded from Android builds (`ANDROID=1`) in `variables.mk` due to the absence of GnuTLS packaging in standard Android runtimes.
- **Kernel Requirements**: Minimum kernel versions align with general eBPF requirements (x86_64 >= 4.18, aarch64 >= 5.5, loongarch64 >= 6.6).
- **Privileges**: Running capture operations requires `root` privileges or `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` / `CAP_BPF` capabilities.

Sources: [AGENTS.md:51-62](), [docs/agent/architecture.md:50-52]()

## Verified Capture Modes and Examples

The GnuTLS probe supports three primary operating modes selected via `-m` / `--mode`: `text`, `keylog`, and `pcapng` [internal/probe/gnutls/config.go:83-91]().

### Text Mode Capture

Text mode intercepts `gnutls_record_send` and `gnutls_record_recv` to decode plaintext application data payloads [internal/probe/gnutls/gnutls_probe.go:204-212]().

```sh
sudo ./bin/ecapture gnutls -m text --gnutlspath /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30
```

**Expected Output:**
```text
[mono_ns=123456789000] PID:1234 TID:1234 Comm:curl WRITE (51 bytes):
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
```

### Keylog Mode Capture

Keylog mode extracts TLS master secrets and direct traffic secrets (including TLS 1.3 traffic secrets) and outputs them in NSS Key Log Format [internal/probe/gnutls/event_masterkey.go:46-60]().

```sh
sudo ./bin/ecapture gnutls -m keylog -l gnutls_keys.log --gnutlspath /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30
```

**Expected Output (`gnutls_keys.log`):**
```text
CLIENT_HANDSHAKE_TRAFFIC_SECRET 0123456789abcdef... 9abcdef012345678...
SERVER_HANDSHAKE_TRAFFIC_SECRET 0123456789abcdef... 9abcdef012345678...
CLIENT_TRAFFIC_SECRET_0 0123456789abcdef... 9abcdef012345678...
SERVER_TRAFFIC_SECRET_0 0123456789abcdef... 9abcdef012345678...
```

### pcapng Mode Capture

pcapng mode combines Traffic Control (TC) packet interception on a specified network interface with embedded TLS Decryption Secrets Blocks [internal/probe/gnutls/gnutls_probe.go:179-186]().

```sh
sudo ./bin/ecapture gnutls -m pcapng -i lo -w gnutls_capture.pcapng --gnutlspath /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30
```

Sources: [internal/probe/gnutls/config.go:153-195](), [internal/probe/gnutls/gnutls_probe.go:175-212](), [internal/probe/gnutls/event_masterkey.go:46-60]()

## 3.1 Choosing Text, Keylog, or pcapng

Selecting the correct mode depends on whether you require immediate plaintext analysis, live packet inspection with Wireshark, or cryptographic key logging [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:66-73]().

| Mode | Representation | Primary Destination Requirement | Typical Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`text`** | UTF-8 Plaintext (Decrypted Read/Write payloads) | Defaults to `stdout`; supports files and networks [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:93-94]() | Immediate terminal inspection, lightweight debugging, script parsing [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:70]() |
| **`keylog`** | NSS Key Log lines (`CLIENT_RANDOM ...`) | Requires explicit destination (`--eventaddr` or `--keylogfile`) [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:94-95]() | Decrypting an independent packet capture (`tcpdump`) in Wireshark [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:71]() |
| **`pcapng`** | Packet blocks + embedded TLS Decryption Secrets Block (DSB) | Requires explicit destination (`--eventaddr` or `--pcapfile`) [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:96-97]() | Single-file packet analysis where packets and decryption secrets are bundled together [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:72]() |

For detailed trade-offs and decision criteria, see [Choosing Text, Keylog, or pcapng](#3.1).

## 3.5 Event Destinations and Rotation

eCapture strictly separates captured event destinations (`--eventaddr`) from operational logs (`--logaddr`) [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:27-30](). Captured payloads and cryptographic secrets are never written to operational logs or error channels [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:27-30]().

- **Supported Sinks**: `stdout`, local files (`file://` or plain paths), ordered TCP connections (`tcp://host:port`), and binary WebSocket streams (`ws://`, `wss://`) [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:44-48](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:120-176]().
- **Rotation Limits**: File-backed text and keylog streams support rotation (`--rotatesize`, `--rotateinterval`), whereas network sinks and `pcapng` streams reject byte-stream rotation policies [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:79-81](), [internal/output/writers/pipeline_test.go:148-149]().

For full syntax options, legacy flag aliases (`--keylogfile`, `--pcapfile`), and channel separation checks, see [Event Destinations and Rotation](#3.5).

Sources: [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:27-104](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:90-176]()

## 3.6 Wireshark Decryption Workflows

Analyzing encrypted traffic via Wireshark can be achieved through two distinct approaches depending on the selected capture mode:

1. **Self-Contained pcapng Workflow**: Open the `.pcapng` file generated by eCapture directly in Wireshark. Because the file contains embedded Decryption Secrets Blocks (DSB), Wireshark automatically decrypts TLS traffic without additional configuration.
2. **Keylog and Packet Capture Workflow**: Run eCapture in `keylog` mode to export an NSS key log file while simultaneously collecting packets via standard utilities like `tcpdump`. In Wireshark, combine the resulting packet capture with the key log file via **Preferences > Protocols > TLS > (Pre)-Master-Secret log filename**.

For step-by-step verification procedures and troubleshooting guidance, see [Wireshark Decryption Workflows](#3.6).

Sources: [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:70-72](), [docs/agent/output-pipeline-refactor-taskbook.md:82-93]()

## 1. Capture Mode Decision Matrix

When configuring a core TLS capture session via `-m` or `--format`, you must choose a representation format that matches your downstream analysis workflow. The following table contrasts the three modes across critical architectural dimensions:

| Dimension | Text Mode (`text`) | Keylog Mode (`keylog`) | pcapng Mode (`pcapng`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Use Case** | Immediate plaintext inspection, terminal debugging, or simple log aggregation. | Decrypting a separate packet capture (e.g., captured via `tcpdump`) inside Wireshark. | All-in-one packet capture containing network blocks and embedded decryption material. |
| **Artifact Content** | UTF-8 formatted plaintext payloads (HTTP, TLS application data transcripts). | NSS Key Log format lines (`CLIENT_RANDOM ...`). | Raw packet blocks combined with a Decryption Secrets Block (DSB). |
| **Destination Rules** | Defaults to `stdout` if empty; supports files, TCP streams, and binary WebSockets. | Requires an explicit destination (`stdout`, file, TCP, WebSocket); truncates files with `0600` permissions. | Requires an explicit destination; generates unframed binary byte streams; rejects byte rotation. |
| **Sensitivity & Security** | Normal sensitivity; logs application text payload directly. | Sensitive; exposes master session secrets capable of decrypting captured traffic. | Sensitive; contains both intercepted raw packets and session decryption keys. |
| **Implementation Entity** | `internal/output/writers.EventFormatText` via `TextHandler` [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:14](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:29]() | `internal/output/writers.EventFormatKeylog` via `KeylogHandler` [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:15](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:30]() | `internal/output/writers.EventFormatPcapng` via `pcapng.Session` [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:16](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:31]() |

## 3. Detailed Mode Analysis

### 3.1 Text Mode (`text`)
Text mode intercepts decrypted application buffers directly from the eBPF uprobe/kprobe hook points and formats them into UTF-8 human-readable strings.
* **Data Flow:** Events are processed by `TextHandler`, which formats payloads using `String()` or `StringHex()` representations without operational-log pollution [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:14](), [cli/cmd/output_pipeline_test.go:36]().
* **Destinations:** By default, text mode targets `stdout`. However, it fully supports redirection to files, TCP listeners, or binary WebSocket streams (`--eventaddr`) [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:68]().
* **Caveats:** Text mode does not capture raw TCP/IP packet headers or underlying framing metadata; it records application-layer payloads and connection tuples as reported by the TLS library hooks.

Sources: [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:14](), [cli/cmd/output_pipeline_test.go:33-46]()

### 3.2 Keylog Mode (`keylog`)
Keylog mode extracts TLS master secrets (e.g., `CLIENT_RANDOM` or TLS 1.3 `EXPORTER_SECRET` / handshake keys) as they are negotiated by OpenSSL, GoTLS, or GnuTLS.
* **Data Flow:** The underlying `KeylogHandler` processes cryptographic key material events and writes them via `KeylogWriter`, which wraps an arbitrary `ByteSink` to ensure strict newline formatting (`\n`) without mutating caller buffers [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:15](), [internal/output/writers/pipeline_test.go:77-104]().
* **Destinations:** Keylog mode requires an explicit destination (or uses the legacy `--keylogfile` alias). Files are created with restrictive `0600` permissions and truncated at startup [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:81](), [docs/agent/output-pipeline-refactor-taskbook.md:109]().
* **Caveats:** Keylog mode **does not contain packet data**. To inspect traffic, you must run a parallel packet capture (such as `tcpdump` or Wireshark) and configure Wireshark to load the generated key log file [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:71]().

Sources: [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:71](), [docs/agent/output-pipeline-refactor-taskbook.md:75-81](), [internal/output/writers/pipeline_test.go:77-104]()

### 3.3 pcapng Mode (`pcapng`)
pcapng mode constructs a standards-compliant PCAP Next Generation capture artifact combining intercepted packet blocks with an embedded Decryption Secrets Block (DSB).
* **Data Flow:** `PcapngSession` manages a single dedicated goroutine running a `pcapgo.NgWriter`. Packet payloads and decryption secrets are queued, ordered synchronously, flushed upon request, and fully drained during shutdown [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:16](), [docs/agent/output-pipeline-refactor-taskbook.md:82-90]().
* **Destinations:** Requires an explicit file path or network destination. Byte-stream rotation (`--rotate`) is strictly prohibited for pcapng streams because it corrupts container framing structures [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:81](), [internal/output/writers/pipeline_test.go:148]().
* **Caveats:** Operational logging (`--logaddr`) and pcapng event streaming (`--eventaddr`) cannot both target `stdout` simultaneously, as intermixing textual log messages corrupts the binary pcapng stream [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:84](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:70-75]().

Sources: [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:16](), [docs/agent/output-pipeline-refactor-taskbook.md:82-94](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:70-75]()

## Purpose and Scope
This page details **Text Mode** (`-m text`), the default operating mode for eCapture's core TLS capture modules (`tls`, `gotls`, and `gnutls`). Text mode intercepts encrypted TLS socket read/write operations via eBPF probes, decrypts or captures payloads in memory, and prints human-readable plaintext events directly to standard output or a designated event address. It is designed for immediate interactive inspection of HTTP requests, responses, and arbitrary application-layer payloads without requiring external packet captures or decryption key files.

## Purpose and Scope
Keylog Mode in `ecapture` is designed to intercept TLS master secrets and ephemeral traffic secrets from user-space libraries (`tls` for OpenSSL/BoringSSL, `gotls` for Go native crypto/tls, and `gnutls` for GnuTLS) without decrypting or capturing packet payloads directly within the eBPF kernel space. Instead, eCapture serializes these cryptographic secrets into the standard **NSS Key Log Format**, outputting them to stdout, a file, or a network sink. 

This mode is ideal for scenarios where packet capture (`pcapng`) overhead must be minimized or where network packets are captured independently via standard network diagnostic tools (such as `tcpdump` or cloud packet mirrors) and later decrypted in analysis tools like Wireshark by combining the packet trace with the exported key log file.

## 2. NSS Key Log Format & Implementation
The core component responsible for formatting and emitting cryptographic secrets is `KeylogHandler` [internal/probe/base/handlers/keylog_handler.go:81](), supported by `KeylogWriter` [internal/output/writers/keylog_writer.go:27](). 

### Supported Secret Types
Depending on the TLS version and library implementation, eCapture handles multiple secret structures:
1. **TLS 1.2 and Earlier (`CLIENT_RANDOM`)**: Emits the 32-byte client random combined with the 48-byte master secret.
2. **TLS 1.3 (`TRAFFIC_SECRET` / Handshake Secrets)**: Emits individual traffic secrets such as `CLIENT_HANDSHAKE_TRAFFIC_SECRET`, `SERVER_HANDSHAKE_TRAFFIC_SECRET`, `CLIENT_TRAFFIC_SECRET_0`, `SERVER_TRAFFIC_SECRET_0`, and `EXPORTER_SECRET`.
3. **GoTLS Label-Based Format**: Utilizes Go's internal secret labels (`CLIENT_HANDSHAKE_TRAFFIC_SECRET`, `SERVER_HANDSHAKE_TRAFFIC_SECRET`, etc.) paired with the client random [internal/probe/base/handlers/keylog_handler.go:54-61]().

## 4. Independent Packet Capture for Wireshark
Unlike `pcapng` mode (which embeds decryption secrets directly inside the packet capture file), Keylog Mode separates packet acquisition from key logging:
1. **Capture Packets**: Record network traffic independently using tools like `tcpdump`:
   ```bash
   tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/traffic.pcap 'tcp port 443'
   ```
2. **Capture Secrets**: Run eCapture in keylog mode:
   ```bash
   ecapture tls -m keylog --keylogfile=/tmp/keys.log
   ```
3. **Decrypt in Wireshark**: 
   - Open `/tmp/traffic.pcap` in Wireshark.
   - Navigate to **Edit > Preferences > Protocols > TLS**.
   - Set **(Pre)-Master-Secret log filename** to `/tmp/keys.log`.
   - Wireshark will automatically use the logged secrets to decrypt TLS sessions on the fly.

Sources: [internal/probe/base/handlers/keylog_handler.go:81-98]()

---

## 5. Sensitive-File Handling and Security Considerations
Because cryptographic keys grant immediate decryption capabilities for recorded or live TLS streams, key log files represent highly sensitive security artifacts:
- **File Permissions**: When using `--keylogfile`, ensure the output file is created with restricted permissions (e.g., `0600`) so that unprivileged local users cannot read master secrets.
- **Storage**: Avoid storing key logs on persistent or world-readable storage volumes; prefer temporary secure directories (`/tmp/`) or streaming over encrypted network sinks via `--eventaddr`.
- **Cleanup**: Purge key log files immediately after analysis sessions conclude.

Sources: [internal/probe/base/handlers/keylog_handler.go:81-131](), [internal/output/writers/keylog_writer.go:51-72]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page covers the technical design, configuration, and operational workflow of eCapture's `pcapng` capture mode (`-m pcap` or `-m pcapng`). This mode records network packets via eBPF probes (such as Traffic Control (TC) filters or socket hooks) and simultaneously captures TLS master secrets from core cryptographic libraries (`tls`, `gotls`, `gnutls`). It serializes both data streams into a single `pcapng` artifact containing standard packet blocks and embedded TLS Decryption Secrets Blocks (DSB). This format allows tools like Wireshark to decrypt HTTPS and TLS traffic automatically without requiring a separate keylog file.

## Interface Selection and Destination Rules

The `pcapng` session initializes by inspecting system network interfaces using `net.Interfaces()` to build interface description blocks (`NgInterface`) [internal/output/pcapng/session.go:84-133](). 

- **Interface Selection (`-i` / `--interface`)**: The interface specified by the user is designated as the primary capture interface (`ifaceIdx`). All other active interfaces are automatically added to the `pcapng` header so that packets originating across bridge or loopback devices map correctly [internal/output/pcapng/session.go:112-148]().
- **Destination Sinks**: Captured data is written to a `ByteSink` abstraction supporting multiple output destinations including local files, TCP streams (`tcp://host:port`), WebSockets (`ws://host:port/`), and in-memory buffers for testing [internal/output/pcapng/destinations_test.go:43-105]().

The flag `--pcapfile` serves as a backward-compatible alias for specifying the output destination path when running in `pcap` or `pcapng` mode. The `Session` struct manages concurrent ingestion of network packets (`TcPacket`) and TLS keylog entries [internal/output/pcapng/session.go:47-76](). ## 1. The Uniform Event Destination Flag (`--eventaddr`)

In `ecapture`, captured domain events are decoupled from operational diagnostic logs. The `--eventaddr` flag (backed by `EventCollectorAddr` in the agent configuration) serves as the sole primary destination selector for captured events across OpenSSL, GoTLS, and GnuTLS capture modules [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:88-91]().

The CLI representation mode (`-m text`, `-m keylog`, `-m pcap` or `-m pcapng`) controls the data encoding format, while `--eventaddr` specifies where those encoded bytes are transported [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:90-91]().

## 2. Supported Sinks (`ByteSink` Sinks)

All raw event destinations implement the `writers.ByteSink` interface [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:33-43](). The interface abstracts underlying transports so that text, keylog, and pcapng handlers write data uniformly without knowing whether the destination is a console, disk file, network socket, or WebSocket stream [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:67-73]().

```go
type ByteSink interface {
    io.Writer
    Name() string
    Flush() error
    Close() error
}
```
*Source: [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:36-41]()*

The `WriterFactory` constructs four distinct transport types based on the URI scheme or destination name provided to `--eventaddr`:

1. **Stdout (`stdout` or empty for text mode)**: Uses `NewStdoutWriter()` to write directly to standard output [internal/output/writers/factory.go:163-164]().
2. **File (`file://...` or a plain filesystem path)**: Uses `NewFileWriter()` to write to local disk with configurable buffering, truncation, and permission settings (`0600` for sensitive keys/pcapng) [internal/output/writers/factory.go:165-168](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:129-137]().
3. **TCP (`tcp://host:port`)**: Uses `NewTcpWriter()` to establish an ordered raw byte stream over TCP [internal/output/writers/factory.go:169-170]().
4. **WebSocket (`ws://...` or `wss://...`)**: Uses `NewWebSocketWriter()` to stream binary WebSocket frames [internal/output/writers/factory.go:171-172](), [pkg/util/ws/client.go:23-36](). Receivers reconstruct the ordered artifact by concatenating frame payloads in arrival order [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:44-48]().

Sources: [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:33-48](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:120-176]()

## 3. Mode-Specific Destination and Rotation Rules

Destination requirements and rotation capabilities vary strictly by capture mode:

| Mode | Default Destination | Explicit Destination Required? | Rotation Supported? | Sensitive Permissions / Truncation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **text** | `stdout` (when `--eventaddr` is empty) | No | Yes (file-backed only) | Standard permissions, append/truncate per config |
| **keylog** | None | **Yes** | Yes (file-backed only) | `0600` permissions, truncated at start [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:81-82]() |
| **pcapng** | None | **Yes** | **No** (rejected during validation) [internal/output/writers/factory.go:105-107]() | `0600` permissions, truncated at start [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:81-82]() |

### Validation & Rotation Limits
* **Network & Pcapng Sinks**: Rotation (`--max-size`, `--max-interval`) is restricted exclusively to file-backed text or keylog streams [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:79-83](). Configuring rotation on a pcapng stream or a network sink (`tcp://`, `ws://`) fails validation during `WriterFactory.ValidateEventSinkAddress()` [internal/output/writers/factory.go:105-116]().
* **Stream Integrity**: Network sinks operate on a strict error policy. A failed connection terminates the stream; intermediate reconnection during an active pcapng artifact is not supported [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:47-48]().

Sources: [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:79-87](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:92-116]()

---

## 4. Legacy Output Aliases and Normalization

To maintain backward compatibility with legacy command-line interfaces, `ecapture` provides alias flags that map directly to the uniform event destination system [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:94-98]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subcode ["Code Entity Space"]
    direction TB
    A["CLI Flags / HTTP JSON Config"] -->|"NormalizeEventAddress()"| B["WriterFactory.ValidateEventSinkAddress()"]
    B -->|"Validates format & aliases"| C["CreateEventSink()"]
    
    style A fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style B fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style C fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
*Figure 2: Normalization and Validation Workflow*

### Aliasing Rules
* `--keylogfile`: Acts as the legacy primary-file alias when operating in keylog mode (`-m keylog`) [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:94-95](). When running in `pcapng` mode, `--keylogfile` functions as a separate, optional secondary keylog artifact while `--eventaddr` (or `--pcapfile`) targets the primary pcapng stream [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:98]().
* `--pcapfile`: Acts as the legacy primary-file alias when operating in pcapng mode (`-m pcap` or `-m pcapng`) [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:96-97]().
* **Conflict Detection**: Explicitly setting both `--eventaddr` and its corresponding legacy primary flag (`--keylogfile` in keylog mode, or `--pcapfile` in pcapng mode) to differing values returns a validation error [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:99-100](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:60-65](). Calling `NormalizeEventAddress()` repeatedly is idempotent [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:103](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:48-66]().

Sources: [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:88-104](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:48-66]()

---

## 5. Separation from Operational Logging (`--logaddr`)

A core architectural invariant in `ecapture` is the absolute separation between operational diagnostics and captured payload data [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:27-29]().

* **Semantic Channels**: 
  - Operational logs (`OperationalLogRecord`) carry status updates, startup warnings, and debugging metrics [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:10-13](). They output by default to `stderr` and optionally fan out to `--logaddr` or eCaptureQ `PROCESS_LOG` [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:10-13]().
  - Captured events (`domain.Event`) carry plaintext payloads, TLS session keys, or network packet blocks [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:14-18](). They route exclusively through event handlers to `--eventaddr` [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:14-18]().
* **Security & Privacy**: Captured plaintext payloads and cryptographic TLS secrets **must never** enter `--logaddr` or eCaptureQ `PROCESS_LOG` [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:27-29]().
* **Channel Collision Prevention**: Binary pcapng streams written to `stdout` cannot share stdout with operational logging. Configuring both operational logging and binary pcapng output to use `stdout` simultaneously is rejected during pre-flight validation via `ValidateChannelSeparation()` [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:84-87](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:70-75]().

Sources: [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:7-30](), [docs/agent/output-pipeline.md:84-87](), [internal/output/writers/factory.go:68-75]()

This page details how to inspect captured TLS traffic using Wireshark through eCapture. It contrasts the two primary Wireshark-compatible analysis workflows supported by eCapture: opening a self-contained `pcapng` capture file with embedded Decryption Secrets Blocks (DSBs) versus combining a standard network packet capture (`pcap`/`pcapng`) with an independent keylog file. It also highlights when utilizing text mode directly in the terminal remains the simpler diagnostic choice.

---

## 1. Embedded Secrets Workflow (`pcapng` Mode)

When eCapture runs in `pcapng` mode (`-m pcapng`), it captures both raw network packets via Traffic Control (TC) probes or socket filters and runtime TLS master secrets via uprobes. It interleaves these events into a single, synchronized stream [internal/output/pcapng/session.go:46-76](). 

The underlying session encoder writes TLS secrets into the stream using Wireshark's standard Decryption Secrets Block (DSB) format before or alongside the chronological packet blocks [internal/output/pcapng/session.go:220-234]().

### Verifiable Steps

1. **Start eCapture in `pcapng` mode**:
   ```bash
   ecapture tls -m pcapng --libssl /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libssl.so.3 -w capture.pcapng
   ```
2. **Generate target TLS traffic** (e.g., using `curl` or a test client against an HTTPS endpoint).
3. **Stop eCapture** (Ctrl+C) to flush buffers and finalize the `pcapng` file [internal/probe/base/handlers/pcapng_handler.go:171-189]().
4. **Open the capture in Wireshark**:
   ```bash
   wireshark capture.pcapng
   ```
5. **Verify decryption**: Wireshark automatically reads the embedded DSB packets, extracts the session keys, and populates the *Transport Layer Security* protocol tree with decrypted application data without requiring external keylog configurations.

## 2. Separate Capture and Keylog Workflow

Alternatively, you can record network packets and TLS master secrets independently. This is useful when network monitoring infrastructure (such as `tcpdump` or dedicated hardware taps) is already deployed, or when you want to feed secrets into an existing packet trace.

### Verifiable Steps

1. **Capture packets using `tcpdump`**:
   ```bash
   tcpdump -i any -w raw_packets.pcap port 443
   ```
2. **Capture TLS keys using eCapture in keylog mode**:
   ```bash
   ecapture tls -m keylog --keylogfile tls_keys.log
   ```
3. **Configure Wireshark**:
   - Open Wireshark and load `raw_packets.pcap`.
   - Navigate to **Edit > Preferences > Protocols > TLS**.
   - In the **(Pre)-Master-Secret log filename** field, browse and select `tls_keys.log`.
   - Click **OK** to decrypt the trace.

## 3. When Text Mode is Simpler

While Wireshark provides deep packet inspection and protocol analysis, `text` mode (`-m text`) is often preferable for quick debugging, container troubleshooting, or automated log ingestion.

* **No Post-Processing Required**: Plaintext HTTP requests, SQL queries, or custom payloads are printed directly to `stdout` or forwarded via `--eventaddr`, eliminating the need to open a GUI or configure decryption keys [internal/probe/base/handlers/pcapng_handler.go:1-55]().
* **Immediate Feedback**: Useful for verifying that uprobes successfully attach to target functions without setting up network capture interfaces.
* **Low Overhead**: Avoids capturing unrelated TCP background noise, framing headers, or stateful packet queues.

Sources: [internal/probe/base/handlers/pcapng_handler.go:32-55]()

## 4. Wireshark Lua Dissector Integration

eCapture includes a custom Wireshark Lua post-dissector plugin (`ecapture.lua`) that injects process metadata (such as PID and command name) into captured packet trailers [utils/ecapture.lua:1-65]().

### Plugin Features
* **Magic Number Validation**: Identifies eCapture-enhanced frames via the magic constant `0xCC0C4CFC` [utils/ecapture.lua:11-51]().
* **Process Enrichment**: Extends the packet details tree to display originating process IDs and command names (`Comm`) [utils/ecapture.lua:16-58]().

To install the plugin for Wireshark:
1. Copy `utils/ecapture.lua` to your personal Wireshark plugins directory (e.g., `~/.local/lib/wireshark/plugins/` on Linux).
2. Restart Wireshark or press `Ctrl+Shift+R` to reload Lua plugins.

## Purpose and Scope

This wiki page provides a comprehensive diagnostic checklist for troubleshooting issues encountered while using eCapture's core TLS modules (`tls` for OpenSSL/BoringSSL, `gotls` for Go native TLS, and `gnutls` for GnuTLS) across all three operating modes (`text`, `keylog`, and `pcapng`). It covers common failure domains including kernel requirements, BPF/BTF support, privilege levels, library/binary mismatches, symbol resolution, interface configuration, and event destination errors.

---

## 1. Kernel Version, BTF, and Privileges Errors

eCapture relies heavily on modern eBPF features, uprobes, and kernel BTF (BPF Type Format) metadata. Startup failures in this domain usually manifest during environment detection [cli/cmd/env_detection.go:74-86]().

### Common Symptoms & Diagnostics
* **Kernel Version Mismatch**: 
  * *Error message*: `the Linux/Android kernel version ... is not supported; require ... or newer` [cli/cmd/env_detection.go:36-38]().
  * *Cause*: Host kernel is older than the architecture minimum (x86_64 requires Linux 4.18+, aarch64 requires Linux 5.5+, and LoongArch64 requires Linux 6.6+) [cli/cmd/env_detection.go:43-54]().
  * *Solution*: Upgrade the host kernel or run on a supported platform.
* **Missing BPF Privileges**:
  * *Error message*: `the current user does not have CAP_BPF to load bpf programs. Please run as root or use sudo or add the --privileged=true flag for Docker` [cli/cmd/env_detection.go:67-69]().
  * *Cause*: Process lacks `CAP_BPF`, `CAP_PERFMON`, or `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` capabilities [cli/cmd/env_detection.go:64-66]().
  * *Solution*: Run with `sudo`, assign capabilities using `setcap` (`cap_bpf,cap_perfmon,cap_sys_ptrace=eip`), or pass appropriate capability flags in Docker [docs/minimum-privileges.md:45-58]() [docs/minimum-privileges.md:79-90]().
* **BTF / Kernel Config Errors**:
  * *Cause*: Neither `/sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux` nor fallback ELF vmlinux files are accessible, and `CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF` is disabled [pkg/util/ebpf/bpf.go:89-98]() [pkg/util/ebpf/bpf.go:118-143]().
  * *Solution*: Ensure your kernel is compiled with BTF support (`CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF=y`) or install kernel debug packages providing `vmlinux`.

## 2. Library, Binary, and Symbol Resolution Mismatches

When eCapture fails to attach uprobes to target binaries or shared libraries, events will not be captured.

### Common Symptoms & Diagnostics
* **Missing Shared Library**:
  * *Cause*: The target OpenSSL (`libssl.so`) or GnuTLS library path cannot be located automatically, or the custom path supplied via `--libssl` does not exist.
  * *Solution*: Specify the absolute path to the shared library using `--libssl` or ensure the application is dynamically linked against a supported library version.
* **Symbol Stripping in Go Binaries (`gotls`)**:
  * *Cause*: The target Go binary was compiled with stripped symbol tables (`-ldflags="-s"`), preventing eCapture from locating internal Go TLS functions and crypto primitive offsets.
  * *Solution*: Recompile or inspect the Go binary without symbol stripping, or use Go module introspection flags to match function offsets.
* **Version Mismatch**:
  * *Cause*: Bytecode assets compiled for OpenSSL 1.1.x are loaded against an OpenSSL 3.x runtime environment (or vice-versa).
  * *Solution*: Ensure eCapture automatically matches or explicitly selects the correct bytecode file corresponding to the target library major/minor version (e.g., `openssl_3_0_0_kern_core.o`) [docs/example-outputs.md:38]().

---

## 3. Empty Events and Missing Secrets

If eCapture starts successfully but produces no plaintext events or decryption keys:

### Checklist
1. **Traffic Generation**: Ensure active HTTPS/TLS traffic is flowing through the targeted process. Idle applications generate no uprobe hits.
2. **Process Targeting (`--pid`)**: If scoping capture to a specific process ID, verify that the PID is correct and that the process is actively initiating new TLS handshakes (existing established connections before eCapture startup will not be decrypted until renegotiated or restarted).
3. **Cipher Suite Support**: 
  * In `pcapng` or `keylog` mode, ensure the cipher suites in use are supported by eCapture's key extraction logic (e.g., non-TLS 1.3 or specific TLS 1.3 key schedule hooks). Unsupported custom crypto libraries or hardware-offloaded cryptographic engines cannot be intercepted via software uprobes.

---

## 4. Incomplete Pcapng & Interface / Traffic Control Errors

When running in `pcapng` mode (`-m pcap` or `-m pcapng`), network packet capture relies on Traffic Control (TC) attachment or network interface packet sniffing.

### Common Symptoms & Diagnostics
* **Missing `CAP_NET_ADMIN`**:
  * *Cause*: Pcapng mode requires TC filters on the specified network interface (`-i`), which demands `CAP_NET_ADMIN` [docs/minimum-privileges.md:13-16]() [docs/minimum-privileges.md:32-33]().
  * *Solution*: Run with `sudo` or add `cap_net_admin` capability [docs/minimum-privileges.md:54]().
* **Invalid Interface Name**:
  * *Error message*: Interface not found or unable to attach TC classifier.
  * *Solution*: Verify available network interfaces using `ip link` and pass the correct interface identifier to `-i`.
* **Missing Secrets Block in Wireshark**:
  * *Cause*: Packets are captured from the network interface, but TLS handshake key extraction failed due to a symbol mismatch in `libssl`, resulting in a pcapng file containing raw encrypted packets without a TLS Decryption Secrets Block (DSB).
  * *Solution*: Confirm that console logs report successful key logger initialization (e.g., `master key keylogger has been set`) [docs/example-outputs.md:30]() and `CLIENT_RANDOM save success` [docs/example-outputs.md:133]().

---

## 5. Destination and Sinks Errors

Operational logs and captured events are routed via distinct configuration parameters.

### Destination Rules & Troubleshooting
* **`--eventaddr` vs `--logaddr`**:
  * `--eventaddr` carries captured payload events (plaintext, key logs, or pcapng byte streams) to stdout, file, TCP, or WebSocket sinks.
  * `--logaddr` carries operational diagnostic logs only. Do not mix up the two endpoints.
* **File Permission and Disk Space Errors**:
  * *Cause*: Writing capture artifacts (`-w output.pcapng` or file-based `--eventaddr`) fails due to insufficient permissions or disk exhaustion.
  * *Solution*: Verify write permissions on the target directory and monitor available disk space, especially during high-throughput pcapng capture sessions.

# TLS 故障排查

## 目的与范围

本页为用户和运维人员提供使用 eCapture 核心 TLS 模块（`tls` 对应 OpenSSL/BoringSSL、`gotls` 对应 Go 原生 TLS、`gnutls` 对应 GnuTLS）以及三种工作模式（`text`、`keylog`、`pcapng`）时的综合故障排查清单。涵盖内核要求、BPF/BTF 支持、权限级别、库与二进制不匹配、符号解析、网卡配置及事件目标错误。

---

## 1. 内核版本、BTF 与权限错误

eCapture 严重依赖现代 eBPF 特性、uprobe 以及内核 BTF（BPF 类型格式）元数据。此领域的启动失败通常出现在环境检测阶段 [cli/cmd/env_detection.go:74-86]()。

### 常见症状与诊断
* **内核版本不匹配**：
  * *错误信息*：`the Linux/Android kernel version ... is not supported; require ... or newer` [cli/cmd/env_detection.go:36-38]()。
  * *原因*：宿主机内核版本低于架构最低要求（x86_64 要求 Linux 4.18+，aarch64 要求 Linux 5.5+，LoongArch64 要求 Linux 6.6+）[cli/cmd/env_detection.go:43-54]()。
  * *解决方法*：升级宿主机内核或在受支持的平台上运行。
* **缺少 BPF 权限**：
  * *错误信息*：`the current user does not have CAP_BPF to load bpf programs. Please run as root or use sudo or add the --privileged=true flag for Docker` [cli/cmd/env_detection.go:67-69]()。
  * *原因*：进程缺少 `CAP_BPF`、`CAP_PERFMON` 或 `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` 权限 [cli/cmd/env_detection.go:64-66]()。
  * *解决方法*：使用 `sudo` 运行、通过 `setcap` 赋予能力（`cap_bpf,cap_perfmon,cap_sys_ptrace=eip`）或在 Docker 中传递相应的特权参数 [docs/minimum-privileges.md:45-58]() [docs/minimum-privileges.md:79-90]()。
* **BTF / 内核配置错误**：
  * *原因*：无法访问 `/sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux` 或备用 ELF vmlinux 文件，且 `CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF` 被禁用 [pkg/util/ebpf/bpf.go:89-98]() [pkg/util/ebpf/bpf.go:118-143]()。
  * *解决方法*：确保内核编译时启用了 BTF 支持（`CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF=y`）或安装提供 `vmlinux` 的内核调试包。

```

    Start["启动 eCapture CLI"] --> CheckKernel["detectKernel() cli/cmd/env_detection.go"]
    CheckKernel -->|内核低于最低版本| ErrKernel["错误：内核版本不支持"]
    CheckKernel -->|内核符合要求| CheckCap["detectBpfCap() cli/cmd/env_detection.go"]
    CheckCap -->|缺少 CAP_BPF / CAP_SYS_ADMIN| ErrCap["错误：权限不足"]

```

## 2. 库、二进制与符号解析不匹配

当 eCapture 无法将 uprobe 附加到目标二进制文件或共享库时，将无法捕获任何事件。

### 常见症状与诊断
* **缺少共享库**：
  * *原因*：无法自动定位目标 OpenSSL（`libssl.so`）或 GnuTLS 库路径，或通过 `--libssl` 传入的自定义路径不存在。
  * *解决方法*：使用 `--libssl` 指定共享库的绝对路径，或确保应用程序动态链接了受支持的库版本。
* **Go 二进制文件符号被剥离 (`gotls`)**：
  * *原因*：目标 Go 二进制文件在编译时带有符号剥离参数（`-ldflags="-s"`），导致 eCapture 无法定位内部 Go TLS 函数和密码学原语偏移量。
  * *解决方法*：重新编译或检查未剥离符号的 Go 二进制文件，或者使用 Go 模块内省标志来匹配函数偏移量。
* **版本不匹配**：
  * *原因*：为 OpenSSL 1.1.x 编译的字节码资产被加载到了 OpenSSL 3.x 运行时环境中（反之亦然）。
  * *解决方法*：确保 eCapture 自动匹配或显式选择与目标库主/次版本相对应的正确字节码文件（例如 `openssl_3_0_0_kern_core.o`）[docs/example-outputs.md:38]()。

---

## 3. 空事件与缺失密钥

如果 eCapture 启动成功，但未产生明文事件或解密密钥：

### 排查清单
1. **流量生成**：确保有活跃的 HTTPS/TLS 流量流经目标进程。处于空闲状态的应用程序不会触发 uprobe。
2. **进程过滤 (`--pid`)**：如果将捕获范围限定为特定进程 ID，请验证 PID 是否正确，并且该进程是否正在积极发起新的 TLS 握手（eCapture 启动前已经建立的存量连接在重新协商或重启之前无法被解密）。
3. **密码套件支持**：
  * 在 `pcapng` 或 `keylog` 模式下，确保所使用的密码套件受 eCapture 密钥提取逻辑支持（例如非 TLS 1.3 或特定的 TLS 1.3 密钥调度钩子）。无法通过软件 uprobe 拦截不受支持的自定义加密库或硬件卸载加密引擎。

---

## 4. 不完整的 Pcapng 与网卡 / 流量控制错误

在 `pcapng` 模式下运行（`-m pcap` 或 `-m pcapng`）时，网络抓包依赖于流量控制（TC）附加或网络接口数据包嗅探。

### 常见症状与诊断
* **缺少 `CAP_NET_ADMIN`**：
  * *原因*：pcapng 模式需要在指定的网络接口（`-i`）上设置 TC 过滤器，这需要 `CAP_NET_ADMIN` 权限 [docs/minimum-privileges.md:13-16]() [docs/minimum-privileges.md:32-33]()。
  * *解决方法*：使用 `sudo` 运行或添加 `cap_net_admin` 能力 [docs/minimum-privileges.md:54]()。
* **无效的网卡名称**：
  * *错误信息*：找不到网卡或无法附加 TC 分类器。
  * *解决方法*：使用 `ip link` 检查可用的网络接口，并向 `-i` 传递正确的网卡标识符。
* **Wireshark 中缺少密钥块 (DSB)**：
  * *原因*：数据包已从网卡捕获，但由于 `libssl` 中的符号不匹配，导致 TLS 握手密钥提取失败，生成的 pcapng 文件仅包含原始加密数据包，而没有 TLS 解密密钥块（DSB）。
  * *解决方法*：确认控制台日志报告密钥记录器初始化成功（例如 `master key keylogger has been set`）[docs/example-outputs.md:30]() 且输出 `CLIENT_RANDOM save success` [docs/example-outputs.md:133]()。

---

## 5. 目标地址与接收端错误

操作日志和捕获的事件通过不同的配置参数进行路由。

### 目标规则与故障排查
* **`--eventaddr` 与 `--logaddr` 的区别**：
  * `--eventaddr` 将捕获的载荷事件（明文、密钥日志或 pcapng 字节流）传输到标准输出、文件、TCP 或 WebSocket 接收端。
  * `--logaddr` 仅传输操作诊断日志。切勿混淆这两个端点。
* **文件权限与磁盘空间错误**：
  * *原因*：由于权限不足或磁盘写满，导致写入捕获产物（`-w output.pcapng` 或基于文件的 `--eventaddr`）失败。
  * *解决方法*：验证目标目录的写权限，并监控可用磁盘空间，特别是在高吞吐量的 pcapng 捕获会话期间。

## Purpose and Scope
This document provides production guidance for deploying and integrating eCapture's core TLS capture modules (`tls`, `gotls`, and `gnutls`). It details event forwarding mechanisms using `--eventaddr` and additive `eCaptureQ` streaming, runtime dynamic configuration via HTTP, sensitive artifact management, and performance evaluation strategies using built-in benchmarking tools.

## 1. Event Forwarding: `--eventaddr` and `eCaptureQ`

eCapture separates operational logging (`--logaddr`), raw captured event streams (`--eventaddr`), and structured real-time publishing (`--ecaptureq`).

### Raw Event Forwarding with `--eventaddr`
The `--eventaddr` flag specifies the destination for the primary captured-event representation selected by capture modes (text, NSS Key Log, or pcapng). 
- **Supported targets**: Standard output, local file paths, TCP sockets (`tcp://host:port`), or WebSocket connections (`ws://host:port/path`).
- **Behavior**: TCP destinations receive an ordered raw byte stream. WebSocket sinks send ordered binary frames that downstream receivers concatenate into a single artifact.

Sources: [docs/event-forward-api.md:34-45]()

### Additive Structured Streaming via `eCaptureQ`
The `--ecaptureq` flag starts a WebSocket server that streams structured runtime logs and captured business events as Protobuf-encoded `LogEntry` messages [docs/event-forward-api.md:46-60](). 

`eCaptureQ` operates additively alongside `--eventaddr`: `--eventaddr` writes the raw format (e.g., pcapng or text), while `eCaptureQ` publishes typed domain events through `pkg/ecaptureq/server.go` [docs/event-forward-api.md:61-71]().

## 2. Runtime Dynamic Configuration via HTTP

eCapture supports updating runtime configuration parameters without restarting the process by exposing an HTTP control server [docs/remote-config-update-api.md:1-21]().

### Enabling and Endpoints
- **Enablement**: Pass the `--listen` flag (e.g., `--listen 127.0.0.1:28256`) [docs/remote-config-update-api.md:6-7]().
- **Endpoints**: All configuration routes are HTTP `POST` requests accepting JSON payloads matching internal configuration structs [docs/remote-config-update-api.md:9-28]().
  - `/tls`, `/openssl`, `/boringssl` — OpenSSL / BoringSSL capture module
  - `/gotls` — Go native TLS capture module
  - `/gnutls` — GnuTLS capture module

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "HTTP Control Plane"
        REQ["HTTP POST /tls"] -->|JSON Payload| PREP["server.go:prepare"]
        PREP -->|Route Match| M["Module Config Update Channel"]
    end

    style REQ fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px

```

### Response Codes
Responses return a unified JSON status structure defined in `cli/http/resp.go` [docs/remote-config-update-api.md:100-119]():

| Code Constant | Value | Description |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `RespOK` | `0` | Configuration successfully accepted and applied |
| `RespErrorInvaildRequest` | `1` | Invalid HTTP request format |
| `RespErrorInternalServer` | `2` | Internal server error |
| `RespErrorNotFound` | `3` | Module resource not found |
| `RespConfigDecodeFailed` | `4` | JSON configuration decoding failed |
| `RespConfigCheckFailed` | `5` | Configuration semantic validation failed |
| `RespSendToChanFailed` | `6` | Internal channel buffer full (retry required) |

## 3. Sensitive Artifact Management and Security

Captured plaintext, NSS key log files, and pcapng files containing embedded TLS Decryption Secrets Blocks carry highly sensitive security data.

- **Storage Permissions**: Benchmark and capture artifact directories must be restricted using strict file permissions (`0700`) to prevent unauthorized local access [docs/performance-benchmarks.md:93-117]().
- **Redaction and Cleanup**: Captured plaintext logs must be reviewed, redacted, and securely purged after analysis. Never commit captured traffic artifacts to version control repositories [docs/performance-benchmarks.md:115-116]().

Sources: [docs/performance-benchmarks.md:93-117]()

---

## 4. Performance Evaluation and Benchmarking

eCapture provides two validation layers for assessing performance overhead and event loss: userspace microbenchmarks and end-to-end kernel benchmarks [docs/performance-benchmarks.md:1-12]().

### Userspace Microbenchmarks
Userspace microbenchmarks measure the OpenSSL userspace decode and text-output pipeline efficiency without loading eBPF bytecode [docs/performance-benchmarks.md:5-6](). Run them using Go test benches:

```bash
go test -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkTLSDataEvent' -benchmem \
  ./internal/probe/openssl
```

Functions such as `BenchmarkTLSDataEventDecode` [internal/probe/openssl/event_benchmark_test.go:29-45]() validate payload throughput and memory allocations per event decode iteration.

Sources: [docs/performance-benchmarks.md:13-31](), [internal/probe/openssl/event_benchmark_test.go:29-45]()

### End-to-End Kernel Benchmarking
The end-to-end benchmark harness (`test/benchmark/tls/run_benchmark.sh`) evaluates real uprobe attachment, perf-buffer ring pressure, decoder dispatch, and file-writer throughput under load [docs/performance-benchmarks.md:7-11]().

Key tunable parameters include:
- `BENCH_MAP_PAGES`: Configures the per-CPU perf reader page count passed to `--mapsize` [docs/performance-benchmarks.md:65-74](). Note that this is a page count, not a byte count (e.g., 8192 pages on 4 KiB page systems equates to 32 MiB per CPU).
- `BENCH_FAIL_ON_LOSS`: Set to `1` to enforce a zero-loss regression gate checking for missing request/response markers or nonzero `perf_lost_samples` [docs/performance-benchmarks.md:67-111]().

Sources: [docs/performance-benchmarks.md:32-137](), [test/benchmark/tls/run_benchmark.sh:1-124]()

## Purpose and Scope

While eCapture's core capabilities focus on TLS interception across OpenSSL, BoringSSL, Go native TLS, and GnuTLS, the platform also provides specialized eBPF probes for non-TLS workloads. These non-core modules extend eCapture's auditing and observability features to shell command execution (Bash and Zsh), alternative cryptographic libraries (NSS/NSPR), and database query monitoring (MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL). 

This page serves as the complete reference for all non-core probe coverage, detailing their supported target binaries and libraries, configuration flags, internal implementation, and event data flows.

## 1. NSS/NSPR Probe

The NSS/NSPR probe captures TLS traffic and cryptographic keys from applications built on Mozilla's Network Security Services (NSS) and Netscape Portable Runtime (NSPR), such as Mozilla Firefox and Thunderbird.

### Supported Targets and Configuration
The probe targets `libnspr4.so` for socket I/O operations and `libnss3.so` for session key derivation. Configuration is managed via `nspr.Config`, specifying paths to the NSS and NSPR shared libraries.

The probe establishes `uprobe` and `uretprobe` attachments on `PR_Write` and `PR_Read` within the NSPR library, alongside hooks for master secret extraction [`internal/probe/nspr/nspr_probe.go:193-224`()]. ## 5.1. TLS Capture Architecture

The `ecapture` agent captures TLS traffic across OpenSSL/BoringSSL (`tls`), Go native TLS (`gotls`), and GnuTLS (`gnutls`) by attaching eBPF programs (uprobes, uretprobes, and TC hooks) to target binaries or shared libraries. The architecture resolves symbols and library paths, extracts payload or key material, and converts kernel-space byte structures into user-space events via perf buffers or ring buffers.

The shared runtime flow connects command execution, factory creation, manager setup, and event decoding as illustrated below:

## 5.2. Probe Framework and Lifecycle

Concrete probes (`openssl.Probe`, `gotls.Probe`, and `gnutls.Probe`) embed `base.BaseProbe` [internal/probe/openssl/openssl_probe.go:46-47]() to inherit shared logging, dispatcher management, reader tracking, and shutdown orchestration. Factory registration occurs during package initialization via Go's `init()` functions, linking CLI commands directly to probe constructors.

The lifecycle follows a strict sequence: configuration validation, initialization, bytecode selection and asset loading via `assets.Asset()` [internal/probe/openssl/openssl_probe.go:126-129](), eBPF manager initialization and attachment, event map retrieval, and reader execution. During teardown, resources are released safely in reverse order.

For details on factory registration, BaseProbe lifecycle hooks, reader tracking, and concurrency management, see [Probe Framework and Lifecycle](#5.2).

## 5.3. Event and Output Pipeline
